items.headline: Why Western pharma is sleeping on China's circular RNA revolution
items.preview: A new podcast discusses the advancements in circular RNA therapeutics in China.
items.article:
RNA therapeutics has had its defining moments, with circular RNA (circRNA) being the next potential breakthrough. CircRNA is more stable than linear mRNA, longer-lasting in the body, and potentially re-dosable. Dr. Lu Gao, CEO of Therorna Inc., discusses the company's advanced circRNA platform and its first-in-human trial.
Why this matters: Western pharmaceutical companies may be overlooking significant innovations in circRNA technology being developed in China, which could reshape therapeutic approaches in the future.

items.headline: Clinical Development Expert has started
items.preview: EpilepsyGTx appoints Dr. Teresa Nunes as CMO to advance gene therapy programs.
items.article:
EpilepsyGTx has appointed Dr. Teresa Nunes as Chief Medical Officer to support its gene therapy program, EPY201, aimed at treating focal refractory epilepsy. Nunes brings extensive experience in clinical development and has previously led medical teams at various organizations.
Why this matters: Her leadership is expected to facilitate the progression of EPY201 through regulatory processes and into early clinical studies, potentially benefiting patients with epilepsy.

items.headline: Most early Alzheimer’s patients receiving anti-amyloid therapy overlook brain-health guidelines, study finds
items.preview: A study reveals that early Alzheimer's patients often neglect lifestyle changes despite therapy.
items.article:
Research from Mass General Brigham Neuroscience Institute indicates that early Alzheimer's patients receiving anti-amyloid therapy, like lecanemab, are not adhering to recommended brain-health guidelines. Only 3% of patients met all 15 recommendations, highlighting a gap between treatment and lifestyle changes.
Why this matters: The findings suggest that access to disease-modifying therapies does not guarantee adherence to lifestyle modifications that could enhance cognitive health, indicating a need for better patient support and education.

items.headline: New platform speeds bacterial gene mapping for better biotech design
items.preview: A new platform enhances bacterial gene mapping, aiding biotech applications.
items.article:
Scientists at Oak Ridge National Laboratory have developed a platform that accelerates the mapping of bacterial genes, enabling the design of microbes for efficient production of chemicals and materials. This method combines synthetic biology and AI to identify genetic triggers for desired traits.
Why this matters: The platform could significantly improve the efficiency of microbial engineering, supporting advancements in biotechnology and domestic production capabilities.

items.headline: Asymmetric chromatin accessibility underlies anterior-posterior axis specification in moth fly embryos
items.preview: A study explores chromatin accessibility in moth fly embryos during axis specification.
items.article:
Research published in PLOS Biology investigates how chromatin accessibility influences anterior-posterior axis specification in moth fly embryos. The study reveals that the anterior determinant, odd-paired, plays a crucial role in driving chromatin accessibility and gene expression during early development.
Why this matters: Understanding these mechanisms could provide insights into evolutionary changes in developmental processes across different species of flies.
